decision.summary: Tenant Jonah Okafor (P-202, vulnerable) is locked out after his front door key snapped in the lock; he says he is safe. I asked him for his DOB by SMS so identity can be verified, sent him the out-of-hours locksmith number and the cost position, and emailed the landlord. The locksmith has not been dispatched: identity is unverified and no visit window is set, so I escalated to maintenance (ESC-105) for tonight's dispatch.

answers.question: 1. Tenant-responsibility lockout or landlord lock fault?
answers.answer: Undetermined. A snapped key could be tenant damage or loss (tenant cost out of hours), but the lock has been stiff since 22 Sep (R-4766, still unassigned), which points to a possible lock fault (landlord). The locksmith's report decides the recharge. Still uncertain: the cause of the snap, whether the stiffness contributed, and the tenant's identity.

answers.question: 2. Options for the tenant tonight and who pays?
answers.answer: (a) Locksmith Hackney Locks 24/7 (C-14, +447700900314) attends once identity is confirmed. Landlord pays if the report finds a lock fault; tenant pays if the key was lost or damaged. (b) Tenant arranges his own locksmith at his cost, with recharge settled later from the report. Nothing is charged to the tenant before the report. The office key safe is only open Mon-Fri 9-17.30 (£50 refundable), so it cannot help tonight.

answers.question: 3. Actions taken?
answers.answer: Requested DOB and welfare check by SMS (REQ-101); sent tenant SMS with locksmith contact and cost position (MSG-102); added note to R-4766 (NOTE-103); emailed landlord Margaret Ellison (MSG-104); escalated to maintenance P1 for dispatch (ESC-105). The locksmith was not booked and no visit window was set.

answers.question: Master key question?
answers.answer: Spare keys are in the office key safe, which is only collectable Mon-Fri 9-17.30 with a £50 refundable deposit. Tonight it is not available. Policy does not allow out-of-hours key collection.

conflicts: Tenant says the lock has been stiff for weeks and he reported it on the portal; the system confirms R-4766 (22 Sep) but it is still at init with no contractor. Treated as a real prior report.
Policy says lost keys are tenant cost, but this is a snapped key, which may be a lock fault. Policy says the locksmith's report decides where cause is unclear, so no charge is assigned yet.
assumptions: No find_tenant or verify_identity tool was available in this run. Identity is therefore unverified, and no tenancy or ticket detail beyond the lockout and R-4766 has been disclosed.
Callout cost has not been quoted. Under the £250 landlord limit, a routine job needs approval, but the lockout is treated as urgent safety-adjacent work for a vulnerable occupant outside at night.
The 'we will not hold you to the cost beyond what the report supports' line in the landlord email is a commitment that the human should confirm.
